clue.text: Bagpipe music Greek character found by Iron Age tower

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
a broch is a round drystone tower of Iron Age Scotland

explanation.surface: A piper plays near an ancient Greek-looking figure beside a prehistoric tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found by' only places one piece beside the other. A BROCH is a round stone tower found in northern Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is the classical, elaborate form of Highland bagpipe composition, theme and variations.

clue.text: Saint featured in Indian art work

indicators.note: featured in says the saint appears within the Indian

parts.note: Patel is a very common Indian surname, standing for an Indian person

explanation.surface: A saint appears in a piece of Indian art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian art' reads as one phrase, but 'Indian' is a person named Patel and 'art work' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a picture drawn with chalky crayons, a work of art.

clue.text: Uncouth old soldiers captured by mistake

indicators.note: captured by means the old soldiers are held inside the mistake

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Rough veterans taken prisoner in error.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is informal British slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Boorish means rude and ill-mannered, which is uncouth.

clue.text: Fall concluded fling

parts.note: over means finished, concluded
to fling is to throw

explanation.surface: An affair has ended and someone has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall' and 'fling' are nouns here: a downfall, and a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: An overthrow is a downfall or defeat, as of a ruler.

clue.text: Impetuous husband regularly sick before and after a drink

parts.note: a drink is a rum

indicators.note: regularly picks alternate letters of sick

parts.note: the same phrase again, a rum, after the sick letters

explanation.surface: A rash husband is often ill before and after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before and after' says A RUM comes both before and after SC, the odd letters of sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Harum-scarum describes someone reckless and impetuous, acting without thinking.

clue.text: Thrust in joke originally in Asian language

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
a jab is a quick thrust or poke

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the following word in

explanation.surface: A dig slipped into a joke, apparently in some Asian tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link joining the thrust to the joke; the second gives its first letter, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Punjabi is the language spoken in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: How the weasel goes for such music!

definitions.meaning: from the nursery rhyme line about the weasel going off with a bang

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme ends 'Pop! goes the weasel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is the noise in the rhyme and short for popular music.

clue.text: Demands massages, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak says the word is to be pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: kneads means rubs and presses muscles, massages

explanation.surface: Someone insists on being rubbed down, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Needs as a noun are requirements, things demanded.

clue.text: Arrive out East with volunteers to set up party machine

indicators.note: out says the east letter leaves the word

parts.note: to appear is to arrive, turn up

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Turning up with volunteers to build a political organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: APPEAR without E is APPAR; TA turned up becomes AT. The Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparat is the administrative machinery of a Communist party.

clue.text: Popular chap right to abandon risqué familiarity

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
Tim is a man's name, a chap

indicators.note: to abandon means the right letter leaves the risqué word

parts.note: racy means risqué, a little indecent

explanation.surface: A well-liked man stops being smutty and becomes close.
explanation.walkthrough: RACY without R gives ACY.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimacy is close personal familiarity with someone.

clue.text: Plant single councillor brought into bar

indicators.note: brought into says the single councillor goes inside the bar

parts.note: to bar is to stop
single means one

explanation.surface: A lone local councillor gets dragged into a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb meaning prevent.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonecrop is a sedum, a fleshy-leaved plant that grows on walls and rocks.

clue.text: Old man or woman, one settled abroad

parts.note: ex means former, old
Pat is a name used by both men and women

explanation.surface: Someone, whatever their sex, has gone to live overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat is an expatriate, a person living outside their native country.

clue.text: George's transparent cloth backing?

definitions.note: read as George is: the 's is a link standing for is

indicators.note: backing says the cloth's name is read from the end to the start

parts.note: toile is a fine sheer linen or cotton fabric

explanation.surface: A question about what lines a man's see-through garment.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist Mary Ann Evans wrote as George Eliot, so George's surname supplies the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the pen name of the Victorian novelist Mary Ann Evans, author of Middlemarch.

clue.text: Confusion conductor revealed about Lassus's first mass

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the conductor goes around the letter

parts.note: a maestro is a distinguished conductor

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of Lassus

parts.note: m is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A conductor causes chaos in revealing a Mass by the Renaissance composer Lassus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revealed' is a link word. Lassus was a Renaissance composer of masses, which makes 'mass' look musical; here it is the physics symbol M.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a violent whirlpool, and figuratively a state of turmoil or confusion.

clue.text: In the plane he finally adapted, like Kala Nag

indicators.note: adapted signals the letters being altered into a new order
finally points to the last letter of he

explanation.surface: An elephant from Kipling is somehow fitted into an aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: INTHEPLANE rearranged by 'adapted' gives ELEPHANTIN, and the last letter of 'he' completes it. Kala Nag is the elephant in Kipling's Jungle Book story 'Toomai of the Elephants'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephantine means of or like an elephant, which Kala Nag is.

clue.text: Cast hear critic's getting nasty typical!

indicators.note: getting nasty suggests the letters turning ugly and out of order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Listen to the reviewer turn vicious, how predictable!
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of critic's stands for is and gives no letter; CAST, HEAR and CRITIC are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Characteristic and typical both mean showing the usual qualities of something.

clue.text: Irritable male involved in current case

indicators.note: involved in says the male is set within the current and case

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a patient is a medical case

explanation.surface: An angry man is caught up in an ongoing lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a lawsuit or a box; it is a doctor's case.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatient means restless and irritable at delay.

clue.text: Train in Chattanooga, producing rhymes for children

definitions.text: Train in Chattanooga, producing rhymes for children

parts.words: Train in Chattanooga, producing rhymes for children
parts.note: the train in the Glenn Miller song about Chattanooga, and a nursery word that repeats itself in rhyme

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chattanooga Choo Choo' was a 1941 Glenn Miller hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A choo-choo is a child's word for a train, as in the famous song.

clue.text: Mayoress accepting ring given by enthusiastic admirer

indicators.note: accepting means the title takes the ring inside it

parts.note: Her Worship is the form of address for a mayoress
a ring is shaped like the letter O
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: The mayoress is handed a ring by a devoted fan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link. In Britain a mayor or mayoress is addressed as Your Worship, so a mayoress is Her Worship; O goes in after HER.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero-worshipper idolises someone, an enthusiastic and uncritical admirer.

clue.text: Spiritual renewal Dan held up in outskirts of Redditch?

indicators.note: in places the Dan word inside the outer letters
outskirts means the first and last letters of Redditch
held up in a down clue means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: Dan was one of the twelve tribes of Israel

explanation.surface: A man named Dan was delayed on the edge of a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns the tribe's name upwards. Redditch is a town in Worcestershire, England; the question mark flags Dan as a tribe, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebirth is a spiritual renewal or regeneration.

clue.text: Authorise printing unit to acquire product

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measure
a power is a number multiplied by itself, a product

explanation.surface: Approving a printing works buying goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to acquire' links the pieces. 'product' is mathematical: a power is a product of repeated factors.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower someone is to authorise them to act.

clue.text: Part of Scotland up in hilly grassland

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards
in says the answer is concealed within these words

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Scotland's high meadows.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading hiLLY GRAssland upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Argyll is a historic county on the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Complaints investigator writing about pal in Arab state

indicators.note: in places the pal and the writing inside the Arab state

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
bud is American slang for a pal

indicators.note: about means the abbreviation for writing is turned round

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A complaints officer writes about a friend living in an Arab country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writing' comes first in the clue but its turned letters follow the pal inside the state; 'about' does the turning.
explanation.definitionFit: An ombudsman is an official appointed to investigate public complaints against organisations.

clue.text: Live with daughter in a comfortable manner

parts.note: well means comfortably, as in living well

explanation.surface: Settling down with a daughter in some comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live in a place, to reside.

clue.text: Thin person making recording

definitions.meaning: to narrow or become thinner towards one end
someone who tapes things, a recorder

explanation.definitionFit: Taper means to narrow, and literally names one who tapes, records sound or video.

clue.text: Suffolk punch? It may get people stoned

definitions.meaning: a Suffolk Punch is a heavy draught breed from eastern England
slang for heroin, a drug that intoxicates its users

explanation.walkthrough: 'punch' looks like a blow or a drink; the Suffolk Punch is a breed of English carthorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Suffolk Punch is a breed of carthorse, and the word is also street slang for heroin.

clue.text: What we may do with time when on holiday

definitions.text: What we may do with time when on holiday

parts.words: What we may do with time when on holiday
parts.note: passing time idly, read also as a phrase saying during a period away from home

explanation.definitionFit: To pass leisure time idly is a phrasal verb; its second word also means absent on a trip.

clue.text: Court duke excluded from deal, perhaps

indicators.note: excluded from says the duke is taken out

parts.note: deal is a kind of softwood timber, an example of wood

explanation.surface: A court where a duke is left out of an arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' looks like an agreement; it is pine or fir timber.
explanation.definitionFit: To woo is to court someone romantically.

clue.text: General loves to tour the lines

indicators.note: to tour means the loves go round the other letters

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O; two loves are OO
L is short for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A general enjoys going round the front lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loves' looks like affection; in tennis love is nil, written as the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the Moorish general in Venetian service in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: Lacking energy he learnt somehow to captivate

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the mixture
somehow signals the letters being worked into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Without much energy, he still learnt how to charm people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges HE LEARNT and 'Lacking energy' says one E is left over, leaving the seven letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthral means to hold someone spellbound, which is to captivate them.
